title: Scientific Foundations of Software Development Coordination Cost Engineering: Modelling, Measurement and Estimation
content: Software development coordination consumes substantial engineering effort, yet coordination cost remains weakly integrated into software engineering economics as an explicitly modelled, measurable, and estimable quantity. To address this gap, the paper pursued the following objectives. First is to develop a generalized engineering model of coordination cost that captures its principal determinants and distinguishes intra-team from inter-team coordination. Second is to establish standardized engineering quantities through which coordination cost can be measured, empirically calibrated, compared, and benchmarked. Third is to develop analytically tractable methods for estimating coordination cost from observable project structure and empirically calibratable parameters. Through a non-empirical deductive methodology, the paper addresses these objectives by establishing the foundations for Software Development Coordination Cost Engineering, providing a systematic framework for coordination cost modelling, measurement and estimation in software development projects.  Coordination is represented as a complex socio-technical dynamical system and decomposed into intra-team and inter-team mechanisms. The framework introduces empirically calibratable unit coordination costs, α and β, measured in engineering-hours per coordination relationship per month, to abstract otherwise analytically intractable contextual dynamics into measurable engineering quantities. A reduced-state representation and closed-form models are then derived to estimate monthly and lifecycle coordination effort from project size, team configuration, and calibrated unit costs. Absolute, Internal Relative, and External Relative Coordination Efficiency measures extend the framework to benchmarking and comparative evaluation.  The outputs establish a continuous engineering chain from modelling and measurement through empirical calibration, analytical estimation, benchmarking, and improvement, and establish the foundations of Software development coordination cost engineering.
